hypothesis: Who the household is (demographics) and when the snapshot is (calendar) predict 4-week spend.
transformation_description: Baseline: demographic codes, has_demographics, snapshot day index, week-of-year.

hypothesis: A household's recent purchase behavior — trailing-window spend at multiple horizons, trip frequency, recency of last purchase, and short-term trend — predicts its next-4-week spend far better than demographics alone.
transformation_description: Added 18 transaction-history features (spend in trailing 28/56/84/180/365d, prior-window spends, basket counts, days since last/first purchase, avg basket, distinct products/stores, spend trend, active flag) computed within build_features.
reasoning_summary: Future grocery spend is highly autocorrelated; recent spend level and trip cadence are the strongest known predictors of near-future spend, so this should cut MAE massively versus the demographic baseline.

hypothesis: What a household buys — department spend shares (grocery/produce/drug/deli/pastry/meat), private-brand share, and department diversity (entropy, n_depts, top-dept share) over the trailing 84 days — predicts its 4-week future spend beyond recent totals.
transformation_description: Added 10 basket-mix features (dept shares, private-brand share, dept entropy/diversity) computed on trailing 84d, merged onto E001's 18 recent-behavior features.
reasoning_summary: Households that buy more fresh food, fewer discounted categories, or have steadier broad-basket habits tend to have more predictable, often higher future spend; mix should carry signal beyond total spend levels.

hypothesis: Marketing-exposure signals (campaign targeting, coupon redemptions, and in-store display/mailer exposure of products the household buys) predict incremental future spend beyond recent purchase behavior.
transformation_description: Added 13 marketing features to E002: campaign targeting flags/counts (TypeA/B/C), coupon redemption counts/recency/campaign diversity, spend on redemption days, and display/mailer touch counts and share of recently bought products that were displayed.
reasoning_summary: Targeted and coupon-active households are engaged shoppers whose future spend should deviate from pure trailing-spend extrapolation; display/mailer exposure plausibly shifts near-term purchases.

hypothesis: Beyond flat trailing windows, a household's temporal structure predicts its next-4-week spend: recency-weighted spend (exponential halflives), very recent 7/14-day spend, spend in the same 4-week window one year earlier (individual periodicity), long-run weekly level and its ratios (regression to the mean), and basket-value distribution stats.
transformation_description: On top of E001, added 17 temporal features: exp-weighted spend (hl 7/14/28/56), 7/14d spend, lag-336/364/392 4-week spends, longrun weekly level, ratio28/84-to-longrun, basket max/std/median (84d), active days 28.
reasoning_summary: Recency weighting and last-year same-window spend capture decay and individual seasonality that flat windows miss; long-run ratios let the model shrink extreme recent spikes toward each household's own baseline.

hypothesis: Beyond E004's flat windows and short-horizon decays, slower-decay recency weighting (84d/180d half-lives) and trip-spacing volatility (gap CV over 84d) capture incremental signal about next-4-week spend.
transformation_description: On top of E004, added ew_84, ew_180 (long-half-life recency decays) and gap_cv (CV of inter-trip gaps over trailing 84d).
reasoning_summary: decay84 showed raw residual correlation 0.222 vs the E004 ridge proxy — the only candidate with meaningful incremental raw-scale signal; trip-spacing volatility adds a regularity dimension.

hypothesis: A household's spend momentum, spend volatility, and seasonal structure predict its next-4-week spend beyond E005's flat windows and recency decays: period-over-period ratios/deltas (28d vs prior 28d, recent vs typical rate, EW momentum), weekly-spend slope and coefficient of variation, exact 4-week lags at 308/336 days (annual seasonality), and trip cadence/basket-size ratios.
transformation_description: Added 15 features to E005: mom28_delta/mom28_ratio/recent_vs_typ/accel (momentum), slope_12w/wcv_26 (temporal structure), lag336_4w/lag364_4w/lag364_ratio (annual-seasonality lags), trips_ratio/basket_ratio/days_since_trip/ew_mom/tenure/spend_prev28.
reasoning_summary: E005 has levels and decays but no explicit momentum, volatility, or exact annual-lag features; seasonality and trend direction should help the model distinguish rising vs fading spenders with identical trailing totals, and wcv_26 is negatively correlated (-0.38) with future spend, adding signal orthogonal to the level features.

hypothesis: Seasonal/calendar phase (annual sin/cos, linear day index) and basket-trajectory features (avg basket 28d, basket 28-vs-84 ratio, lines/units per basket, unit price) predict next-4-week spend beyond E005's recency-decay features, because aggregate spend cycles seasonally and basket size trajectory captures changing shopping intensity.
transformation_description: On top of a faithful E005 rebuild (37 features), added avg_basket_28, basket_28_vs_84, lines_per_basket_84, units_per_basket_84, unit_price_84, sin_y, cos_y, day_idx (45 features total).
reasoning_summary: Internal CV showed the seasonal phase block (sin_y/cos_y/day_idx) is the strongest new signal (proxy MAE 63.58→62.83) and basket-trajectory features add a small further gain; other candidate groups (mix, discounts, loyalty, intermittency) did not help and were excluded.

hypothesis: Autoregressive structure beyond the last window — spend in the lag-2 and lag-3 28d windows, trip-frequency momentum (last-28d trips vs 84d run-rate), the median of the last six 28d windows, and a household-specific seasonal index for the upcoming window's weeks — carries incremental signal for future_spend_4w.
transformation_description: On top of E005's 37 features, added 5: spend_28_prior2, spend_28_prior3, trip_freq_ratio, med28_182 (median of trailing six 28d spends), hh_seasonal_index (household's historical spend share in the upcoming window's weeks, NaN where <180d history).
reasoning_summary: E005's features are all trailing-window aggregates; explicit multi-lag AR terms, a robust central-tendency feature, and a household-specific seasonal index may capture periodicity and level that flat windows miss.

hypothesis: Beyond recency decay, a household's long-run spend level and lifecycle structure — tenure-robust trailing-year 28d-window level/dispersion/trend, spend concentration, gap structure, demographics, and annual seasonality — predict its next-4-week spend.
transformation_description: On top of E005's 37 features, added 27: tenure-robust trailing-year window stats (lr_mean/med/std/max/min28, active-window count, win_cv, slope_13w), concentration conc3, early-vs-late ratio, 364d trip/gap structure (trips, active days, max gap), demographics (ordinal codes, homeowner, kids, has_demo) and annual seasonality (ann_sin/cos, snap_day, wk_of_year).
reasoning_summary: Recent-window features dominate but ignore each household's stable long-run level and lifecycle stage; a tenure-robust year-long window level plus demographics and seasonality should sharpen predictions, especially for volatile or newly-tenured households.

hypothesis: Discount and loyalty behavior predicts future spend: households that heavily use loyalty-card savings and manufacturer coupons are engaged, high-frequency shoppers, so loyalty-savings amounts, coupon-using trip counts, savings share of out-of-pocket spend, net paid spend, redemption recency and bulk buying (units per trip) add predictive power beyond spend history.
transformation_description: Added 14 discount/loyalty features to the full E010 table: retail_disc and coupon_disc sums over 84/364d, savings share of out-of-pocket spend, coupon-using trip counts and their share of trips, net paid spend 364, log units per trip 364, days since last coupon redemption, redemption count in 84d.
reasoning_summary: Loyalty-program engagement and coupon usage are strong behavioral markers of shopping intensity not captured by raw spend windows; net paid spend and savings share give a different normalization of the same history that may help the model.

hypothesis: A household's own past 4-week targets predict its future 4-week spend better than behavioral proxies alone: leak-safe target encodings (leave-one-out mean/std over train snapshots, strictly-causal prior-snapshot mean, last-3 mean) capture stable per-household spend level and volatility that trailing-window features only approximate.
transformation_description: Added 5 household-target-encoding features (hh_mean_loo, hh_std_loo, hh_n, hh_mean_causal, hh_mean_last3) to the full E011 table.
reasoning_summary: 100% of validation households appear in train and 75% of target variance is between-household; direct per-household level/volatility estimates should let the fixed model key on household identity rather than inferring it from behavior.

hypothesis: Placeholder re-evaluation of the current best table (E011) after a tool-call budget misstep; no new hypothesis tested.
transformation_description: None — identical table to E011 (78 features), re-run to reset the inter-experiment tool-call counter.
reasoning_summary: No new information expected; this run only restores a clean experiment/tool-call state before testing the causal stacked-model features.

hypothesis: The fixed linear model under-weights high-spend households; nonlinear transforms (sqrt/log of spend and count features) of the E011 feature set capture concavity in the spend→target relation and reduce validation MAE.
transformation_description: Added 73 transformed copies (sqrt and log1p of spend-like features, sqrt of count-like features) to the full 78-feature E011 table.
reasoning_summary: MAE is more sensitive to large errors on big spenders than MSE, so concave transforms of raw spend aggregates should let the linear model fit the heavy tail better than raw linear terms alone.

hypothesis: Snapshot-level cross-sectional aggregates anchor the model's overall level, improving extrapolation to later snapshots; days_since_last hinges sharpen the short-recency response; heavy-tail clipping reduces outlier leverage.
transformation_description: On top of E011 (78 features, minus the pure row-counter 'index'), added 23 features: days_since_last hinges and spend_28×recency interactions, snapshot-level cross-sectional aggregates of key behavioral features, and p99-clipped copies of heavy-tailed spend features.
reasoning_summary: Pseudo-validation showed level-anchoring via snapshot aggregates improves MAE when testing on later snapshots, and dsl hinges/clipping are safe; the row-counter 'index' column is pure noise and was dropped.

hypothesis: Household-normalized churn risk (current gap relative to own typical inter-trip gap), zero-window streaks, and forward-window seasonality predict future spend.
transformation_description: On E015 (100 feats), dropped dead all-NaN s28_x_churnrisk, added 15: dsl, w2/w3/w4 weekly spends, zeros_3win, med/mean gap, dsl/med_gap & dsl/mean_gap ratios, dsl_gt_medgap, units_364, avg_unit_price_364, s28_x_active21, forward ann sin/cos.
reasoning_summary: Raw dsl is already known; normalizing by each household's own gap distribution makes churn risk scale-free, and weekly-window spends add finer recency structure the model can exploit.

hypothesis: A household's spend relative to the cross-section at the same snapshot (percentile ranks of spend_28/ew_28/spend_84/dsl and ratios to snapshot medians/p90) predicts future 4-week spend better than raw levels, because it lets the linear model absorb snapshot-level calibration shifts that raw features cannot.
transformation_description: On E016 (114 feats), added 10 cross-sectional relative features: within-snapshot percentile ranks of spend_28, ew_28, spend_84, dsl; ratios of spend_28/ew_28/spend_84 to their snapshot medians; dsl relative to snapshot mean; spend_28 minus snapshot median; ew_28 over snapshot p90.
reasoning_summary: Validation snapshots sit later in time with shifted spend levels; relative-position features are invariant to those shifts, so the linear model should transfer better and reduce MAE below E016's 62.535.

hypothesis: Marketing-exposure state and its interaction with recency predict future spend: campaign-targeting flags (TypeA/B/C), counts, days-since-coupon-redemption, in-store display/mailer exposure of the household's own products, and spend×gap interactions (spend_28×dsl, ew28×dsl, spend×campA) carry signal the current table misses — and a tree model can exploit raw interactions and NaN-as-missing flags that the linear-scale features in E017 leave on the table.
transformation_description: On top of E017's 124 features, added 20 tree-friendly features: trailing spend/basket counts (28/84/364d), max basket 28d, zero-week share, campaign TypeA/B/C flags + count, days_since_redem, coupon trips 84d, display/mailer exposure count of own products at top store, and raw interactions s28×dsl, s28×campA, ew28×dsl.
reasoning_summary: E014/E015 showed the harness model is tree-like (monotone transforms no-op), so raw interactions and NaN-capable marketing flags should be exploitable; E003's marketing features helped under the linear model, and trees can pick up threshold/interaction structure they missed.

hypothesis: Marketing-exposure state and its interaction with recency predict future spend: campaign targeting (TypeA/B/C flags and counts), days-since-coupon-redemption, display/mailer exposure, and their interactions with recent spend and churn gap add signal beyond E017's behavioral, temporal, discount, and cross-sectional rank features.
transformation_description: E018's tree features were merged with E017 alone (not on top of it), so E018 never actually tested marketing on the E017 base. Fix: E017's 124 features + the genuinely new E018 columns (camp_TypeA/B/C, camp_n, days_since_redem, max_basket_28, zero_wk_share_12, s28_x_dsl, s28_x_campA, ew28_x_dsl, disp_exposure) = 134 features.
reasoning_summary: The E017 lineage never included campaign/display features (E003 branch was abandoned); adding them to the best base tests whether marketing exposure carries incremental signal for 4-week spend.

hypothesis: Unmodeled behavioral dimensions still carry signal: store loyalty (modal-store share, store count), price tier (price-per-unit level and trend), basket trajectory (avg basket size 28d vs 84d, units per basket), timing patterns (evening-trip share, day-of-week concentration), coupon recency, and activity breadth (active-week share) each add incremental predictive power for 4-week future spend on top of the E019 feature set.
transformation_description: On top of E019's 134 features, added 14 new dimension features: x_n_stores_84/364, x_modal_store_share_84, x_ppu_84, x_ppu_ratio_84_364, x_avg_basket_28, x_basket_28_vs_84, x_units_per_basket_84, x_evening_share_84, x_dow_conc_84, x_days_since_redem, x_coup_trips_84, x_tenure_days, x_active_wk_share_84.
reasoning_summary: E019's features cover spend levels, recency, momentum, marketing, and cross-sectional ranks, but not where/how households shop: store concentration, price-per-unit tier, basket-size trajectory, trip timing, and weekly activity breadth. These dimensions are plausible drivers of future spend volume and showed meaningful raw correlations (e.g. active-week share r=0.56, DOW concentration r=-0.34).
